text:
sasha: Heads-up: Product wants to launch halo-v2 next Tue 09:00 UTC (gradual rollout over 48h). We need a quick projection for tokens/sec, GPU-hours, and any region constraints. Can infra folks sketch worst-case and canary-to-prod scaling?

jordan: Canary numbers from last 24h (small user cohort): avg tokens/request = 520, avg requests/sec = 18, peak rps ~55, p95 latency = 340ms. Also saw request rate ~1.9x baseline for similar model.

lee: Useful. If we scale to full prod with 15M DAUs and conservative 0.25 requests/user/day -> ~3.75M requests/day. Using 520 tokens/request -> ~1.95B tokens/day.

maria: Quick calc to get tokens/sec: 1.95e9 / 86400 ~= 22,569 tokens/sec sustained. Peak could be 3x sustained -> ~67.7k tokens/sec.

jordan: From perf bench: a 80GB accelerator (prod config) sustained decode throughput for halo-v2 ~7,500 tokens/sec when serving mixed batch sizes and our batching latency SLOs. So rough per-GPU capacity = 7.5k tps.

lee: So baseline sustained need = 22,569 / 7,500 ~= 3.01 GPUs -> round up = 4 GPUs to cover sustained. For peak headroom 67,700 / 7,500 ~= 9.02 -> round up = 10 GPUs.

sasha: That matches my napkin math. We also need to account for safety (node failures, rolling updates, capacity fragmentation). Recommend +25% buffer on top of peak -> 10 * 1.25 = 12.5 -> 13 GPUs in target region.

tim: Region split: product traffic expected 65% US-WEST, 25% EU-WEST, 10% APAC. If we distribute peak 67.7k accordingly -> US-WEST ~44k, EU ~16.9k, APAC ~6.8k. GPUs by region (peak w/o buffer): US-WEST 44k/7.5k=5.9->6, EU 2.25->3, APAC 0.9->1. With 25% buffer -> US 8, EU 4, APAC 2 (total 14).

maria: Note: Dedicated customers may pin older model variant (halo-v1 quantized) which uses ~3.5k tps/GPU — if a non-trivial fraction falls back we'll need to account for mixed flavors on same pools (scheduling complexity).

infra-bot: deploy-canary: Canary rollout completed at 1769300500. Observed instance saturation events: 2 spikes where queue latency > 500ms for ~90s.

jordan: Those spikes correspond to networking hiccups in eu-west AZ-a (packet loss/latency). We should treat eu-west capacity as fragile for first 72h.

lee: Action items: 1) Provision +6 GPUs in US-WEST, +3 in EU-WEST, +2 in APAC as hot capacity (total 11). 2) Reserve additional cold GPUs to instantly attach for spikes: +4 (regional split 2/1/1). 3) Enable autoscaler threshold at 70% GPU token/sec utilization and 2s queue latency trigger.

sasha: Cost estimate: hourly cost per GPU (cloud list) = $3.60 (amortized infra rate). Hot GPUs 11 -> 11 * 24 * 3.6 = $950.4/day. Cold reserve (4) kept stopped with warm images ~ $0.1/day each -> negligible. Monthly approx $28.5k for hot fleet.

tim: Can we use transient spot for the cold buffer? If network instability triggers allocation delays, cold-to-hot attach time ~4–6 minutes on average. That buys acceptance for short bursts.

maria: One more risk: token distribution skew — if a small subset of users generate long outputs (e.g., chat sessions with 2–4k tokens), effective tokens/request could double. If avg_tokens/request = 1,000 then sustained becomes 43k tps -> ~6 GPUs sustained and peak ~130k -> ~18 GPUs peak. Keep that scenario in triage.

jordan: TL;DR concrete ask to SRE: provision 11 hot GPUs across regions (8 US, 2 EU, 1 APAC) and keep 4 cold (2 US,1 EU,1 APAC) ready. Enable autoscaler at 70% and circuit-breaker fallback to halo-v1 if latency > 1s for >60s.

sasha: Thanks. Can someone create the infra ticket with these numbers + cost estimate and tag @oncall for the 48h launch window? :thumbsup:

lee: Filing now -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4218 (added the capacity table, cost calc, and rollback plan).

infra-bot: ticket-created: INFRA-4218 by lee at 1769301205.

maria: I'll run a quick model-variant traffic simulation in the sandbox to validate mixed-flavor scheduling impact and post results by EOD.

sasha: Perfect — will review. If any of you see the eu-west networking alerts escalate, DM me immediately.

tim: Noted.

lee: Closing thread after actions are reflected in INFRA-4218.
